title: UFold-X: an enhanced Dual & Dynamic U-Mamba model for long-range RNA secondary structure prediction.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed the public Google Drive folder: 16 dataset files (.cPickle/.pickle) and 8 model-weight files (.pt), no login needed. Downloaded RCSB1800.cPickle (4.21 MB) and RCSB4000.cPickle (18.26 MB) and read them with a restricted unpickler (no code execution): RCSB1800 = exactly 40 records, sequence lengths 611-1799 nucleotides; RCSB4000 = exactly 61 records, lengths 2821-4810. Each record holds a one-hot sequence array (1800x4 or 5000x4, zero-padded), a 3-column structure-label array, the true length, a PDB-derived file name (e.g. 8T2S-2D-bpseq.txt) and an explicit base-pair list (10-2812 pairs). Got byte sizes of the other 12 dataset files by HTTP HEAD and estimated record counts from the constant per-record size: RNAstralign_train_1800 ~9,342 and test ~1,099 (paper says 8,793 / 1,035), BGSU1800 ~644/162, BGSU5000 ~1,243/311, Rfam1800 ~1,019/255, Rfam5000 ~1,660/416. Read the GitHub README (states 20-40 GB GPU memory for training, CUDA-only mamba-ssm wheel, ~2 h per test set) and the full text from PMC13569499.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The 30,451-sequence RNAstralign total, the ArchiveII count (3,975), the 12,711 RNA Mapping Database chemical-reactivity constructs for the UFold-X-R reactivity variant, the 66-sequence cross-clan test set and the 161-sequence cross-family test set, and all reported accuracy numbers (cross-family F1 0.495 vs CONTRAfold 0.444 vs UFold 0.389). None of ArchiveII, RNAstralign-600, RNAstralign-all, the chemical-reactivity data, the cross-clan test set or the cross-family test set is present in the released Drive folder, even though the repository's data README claims all testing data is there.

a1_downloadable.note: Public Google Drive folder, no login: I listed all 24 files and downloaded two of them. Caveat: the headline cross-clan and cross-family test sets and ArchiveII are not in the folder despite the README saying they are.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The label is in the file: each record carries an explicit base-pair list (verified, e.g. 338 pairs for PDB entry 8T2S) plus a structure-label array, so the paired-partner target needs no construction across sources.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequences are stored as one-hot arrays inside the same records (verified shapes 1800x4 and 5000x4); no accession lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Structure labels are nucleotide index pairs, which are unambiguous. Noted separately: the SHAPE (selective 2'-hydroxyl acylation) reactivity variant uses normalised reactivity in arbitrary units that differ between experiments, but that data is not released here.

a5_enough_rows.note: Aggregate rows are sufficient: RNAstralign_train_1800 ~9,342 records estimated from file size (paper says 8,793). But the long-RNA contribution itself is tiny and mostly redundant: 40 + 61 Protein Data Bank structures verified exactly, 66 cross-clan test sequences per the paper.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~3.1 GB of pickles on disk, but 17-channel L-by-L input tensors: 1.7 GB per sequence in float32 at L=5000
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL. The baseline needs a GPU three ways: the authors' own README states 20-40 GB of GPU memory for training; mamba-ssm (the state-space kernel the model is built on) ships CUDA-only wheels and the README insists the CUDA/torch versions match; and one test set takes ~2 hours on their GPU. The model's input is a 17-channel length-by-length matrix, so a single 5,000-nucleotide RNA is 1.7 GB in float32 before any U-Net activations, far past 16 GB of CPU RAM. No streaming or subsetting route exists, because the long sequences are the whole point of the paper.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: RCSB1800 = 40 and RCSB4000 = 61 records match the paper exactly, and size-based estimates for RNAstralign (~9,342 / ~1,099) sit within ~6% of the stated 8,793 / 1,035. Mismatch is in coverage, not counts: files the README promises are absent.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL for the paper's headline benchmark. For the cross-clan experiment the authors mutate 5-10% of bases to make 2,640 artificial sequences, then write: 'we apply CONTRAfold ... and treat the predicted structures as reference labels'. So the flagship long-RNA training labels are another model's output, which caps the model at CONTRAfold's accuracy and explains why it lands 'comparable to classical approaches'. The PDB-derived labels I opened are fine (base pairs annotated from experimental 3D structures by RNApdbee 2.0), and RNAstralign labels come from comparative sequence analysis, which is itself an inference rather than a direct measurement.

existing_models.name: UFold-X (this paper's own model; a convolutional U-Net plus a Mamba state-space branch)
existing_models.score_and_split: F1 (harmonic mean of precision and recall on predicted base pairs) 0.495 on a 161-sequence cross-family split vs CONTRAfold 0.444 and UFold 0.389; on the 66-sequence cross-clan split, only 'comparable to' classical thermodynamic methods. I verified 8 weight files exist in the Drive folder but did not run them.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They state that models trained on few Rfam clans are 'prone to severe performance degradation' on structurally novel RNA classes, and that long-RNA training data is scarce - which is why they fell back on CONTRAfold-generated labels.

existing_models.name: UFold (2022, Nucleic Acids Research; the predecessor U-Net)
existing_models.score_and_split: Self-reported F1 0.654 on the RNAstralign test split and 0.91 on ArchiveII, both same-family splits that are now known to be inflated.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Long sequences: limited receptive field, which is the gap UFold-X claims to fill.

existing_models.name: sincFold (2024, Briefings in Bioinformatics; convolutional network with short- and long-range blocks)
existing_models.score_and_split: Median F1 0.911 on ArchiveII and, per its authors, the best deep-learning generalisation under family-fold cross-validation (each RNA family held out in turn), improving on 5 of 9 families.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Cross-family generalisation remains well below within-family performance.

existing_models.name: MXfold2 (2021, Nature Communications; deep network regularised by thermodynamic folding energies)
existing_models.score_and_split: Evaluated on ArchiveII and bpRNA-new, the standard splits UFold-X also reports against.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Pure learned models overfit families; hence the thermodynamic regulariser.

existing_models.name: Szikszai et al. 2022, Bioinformatics - 'Deep learning models for RNA secondary structure prediction (probably) do not generalize across families'
existing_models.score_and_split: Showed F1 falling ~36% when moving from within-family to between-family test sets; this is the honest re-evaluation of the whole field, already published.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Whether any sequence-only deep model can fold an unseen family at all.

existing_models.name: RibonanzaNet (2024, Das lab, Stanford; transformer trained on chemical-mapping data)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on 2.1M crowd-sourced RNA sequences with DMS and 2A3 chemical mapping (806,578 released for the Kaggle competition); also predicts secondary structure.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Pseudoknots and long transcripts beyond the ~450-nucleotide training length.

backbone.name: None that fits. RNA-FM and RiNALMo (RNA language models) cap at ~1,022 nucleotides, which excludes the 600-5,000 nucleotide regime that is this paper's entire contribution; RibonanzaNet was trained on ~450-nucleotide constructs.
backbone.hardware: Authors' own README: 20-40 GB GPU memory for training, CUDA-only mamba-ssm, ~2 h per test set.
backbone.licence: Code CC-BY-4.0 on Zenodo; weights shared on Google Drive without a stated licence.

integration.partner_dataset: Rfam 15.0 clan annotations and the Protein Data Bank / RNAsolo representative sets, which the paper already uses.
integration.join_key: PDB identifier (the file names carry it, e.g. 8T2S) and Rfam family/clan accession.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does accuracy on long RNAs fall with evolutionary distance from the training clan - a good question, but the usable test material is 40 + 61 + 66 highly redundant, mostly ribosomal structures, and the published cross-family work already answers it.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: predicted base pairs must be Watson-Crick or wobble, and the model should nail 5S and 16S ribosomal RNA, which dominate these sets.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is runnable, but only on a GPU.
controls.external_validation: The PDB-derived sets (RCSB, BGSU, Rfam-from-RNAsolo) are three overlapping views of the same Protein Data Bank entries, so they are not independent of each other; genuine external validation would need bpRNA-new or Rfam clans not in training.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'among long RNAs whose 3D structures are already in the Protein Data Bank - overwhelmingly ribosomal RNA - a Mamba-based network predicts base pairs about as well as thermodynamic folding does, when trained on sequences whose labels came from a thermodynamic folding program.'

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an RNA sequence to predict which of its nucleotides pair with which, for long RNAs over 600 nucleotides.
plain_idea.train_on: One-hot encoded RNA sequences padded to 1,800 or 5,000 nucleotides; I verified ~9,342 training records for the 600-1,800 nucleotide set and 40 + 61 exact records for the two Protein Data Bank sets.
plain_idea.predict: A pairing partner for every nucleotide (a contact matrix). True answers come either from 3D structures solved by crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy and annotated by the RNApdbee tool, or from comparative sequence alignments - and, for the headline cross-clan benchmark, from the CONTRAfold program's own predictions.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Reliable folding of long RNAs would help anyone studying long non-coding RNAs or viral genomes, but the honest finding here is that the released material cannot support a new long-RNA model on a laptop.

more_or_better_data.why: The training material is the same RNAstralign/ArchiveII/PDB pool every competitor uses (~8,793 sequences for the long split), and the long-RNA extension adds only 40 + 61 verified PDB structures plus PDB re-slices. For chemical-reactivity modelling, RibonanzaNet's 806,578 released sequences dwarf the 12,711 constructs used here.

confidence_score.why: There are no replicate structure determinations per sequence in the released pickles - one structure label per record - so per-prediction uncertainty cannot be calibrated from this data.

models_beatable.why: sincFold (2024) and MXfold2 (2021) are open and already evaluated with family-fold cross-validation, and Szikszai et al. (2022, Bioinformatics) published the honest cross-family re-evaluation of the whole field. The crowded-field exception needs reproducible models to be absent or dishonestly evaluated; here they are neither.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition outright: UFold-X cannot be run as our baseline without CUDA and 20-40 GB of GPU memory, so there is no shared starting point to improve on.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: train or re-evaluate a long-RNA base-pair predictor on the released pickles (which are genuinely feature/label ready, with sequences and explicit pair lists in one record). It dies on compute - 17-channel length-by-length tensors, 1.7 GB per 5,000-nucleotide sequence, and a CUDA-only state-space kernel - and on label provenance, since the flagship cross-clan training labels are CONTRAfold predictions rather than measurements.

effort.compute_note: Disk size measured by HEAD on all 14 remaining files (3.1 GB total) plus the two I downloaded. Peak RAM is the authors' own stated 20-40 GB of GPU memory; the 1.7 GB-per-sequence input figure is my arithmetic (17 channels x 5000 x 5000 x 4 bytes), and the pickles actually store float64, doubling it. The 120-minute figure is the README's own per-test-set time on their GPU, not timed by me.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the non-redundant long RNAs that carry an experimentally derived structure. Done: 40 (RCSB1800) + 61 (RCSB4000) verified in the files, plus 66 cross-clan test sequences from the paper - and the BGSU, Rfam and RCSB sets are three overlapping slices of the same Protein Data Bank entries, mostly ribosomal RNA.

verdict_reason: Fails A6: the baseline requires a GPU with 20-40 GB of memory by the authors' own README, needs CUDA-only mamba-ssm, and feeds 17-channel length-by-length tensors that reach 1.7 GB for a single 5,000-nucleotide RNA - no streaming route exists because long sequences are the point. Also fails A8: the headline cross-clan benchmark trains on CONTRAfold's predicted structures as 'reference labels', so the model distils a thermodynamic program rather than learning from measurements. Secondary reasons: the experimentally grounded long-RNA material is 40 + 61 Protein Data Bank structures (verified exactly) plus a 66-sequence cross-clan test set, all dominated by ribosomal RNA and overlapping across the BGSU/Rfam/RCSB slices; the released Drive folder omits ArchiveII, the cross-clan set and the cross-family set that the README promises; and the field is saturated with open, honestly evaluated models (sincFold, MXfold2, plus Szikszai et al. 2022, which already published the cross-family re-evaluation).
